articleTitle: Wearable Knee Cap Microwave Sensor for Osteoarthritis Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a common musculoskeletal disease that causes joint deterioration, primarily in the knee and hip joints. With the rising ageing population and obesity rates, it has become a significant global public health concern. To address this, there is a growing demand for smart textiles that can incorporate wearable antenna sensors directly on the body for sensing and communication purposes. In our study, we designed a highly efficient monopole antenna on a flexible nylon substrate fabric known for its exceptional elasticity. The antenna was constructed and numerically simulated to achieve optimal performance. The monopole antenna is intended for use at 2.45 GHz in the Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. A human knee model is constructed and examined for the effects of healthy and osteoarthritic knees on the resonance frequency where the change in the antenna's peak resonating frequency can be used to diagnose knee osteoarthritis in a non-invasive manner.

articleTitle: Asymptotic Solution of the Scattering Problem on a Set of Chaotic Placed Small Particles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper, we study the electromagnetic (EM) field scattering on a set of chaotic placed small particles using the asymptotic method. Initially, the particles are embedded in a homogeneous material with the fixed material parameters. The smallness of particles results in the semi-analytical form of solution, which in the numerical relation is reduced to solving the system of linear algebraic equations (SLAE) with respect to the auxiliary parameters. This defines an explicit solution to the problem of scattering. The new physical result is the magnetic permeability specific distribution in the obtained inhomogeneous material. The explicit relation is reduced for this material parameter as well.

articleTitle: Study of Contact Drying Granular Materials in Fluidized Bed Dryers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A model of conductive drying a layer packed with granular capillary-porous material is presented. On its basis, the problem of thermo-moisture-mechanics is formulated. A system of essentially nonlinear differential equations is obtained and a methodology for their solution is proposed. On the basis of the obtained solutions, a computer analysis of the influence of the external heat flow, initial moisture saturation on temperature change, volumetric moisture saturation, and air density in the pores of the body over time has been carried out by the example of conductive drying.

articleTitle: Amplitude Synthesis Problems for the Case of Simple Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The amplitude synthesis problem of the antenna synthesis theory results in the specific form of the reduced nonlinear integral equations. The form of such equation can vary depending on the operator describing the calculation of radiation pattern of antenna; an operator corresponding to linear antenna is considered in the paper. The methods of successive approximations are applied for solving the obtained equations. The non-uniqueness of solutions is characteristic feature of the equation under consideration. The correctness of analytical derivations is approved by the numerical calculations; the definitive fact is that the proposed iterative procedures provide fast convergence.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model of E-polarized Wave Diffraction on a Reflecting Non-PEC Stripe System Above the Screen
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Integral equations describing the process of reflection of electromagnetic waves from a structure consisting of a non-PEC system of strips located over a conducting screen were obtained. The PR-method for deriving this system of equations has been applied. Results of computer experiments for structures with various numbers of strips per period are presented.

articleTitle: Problems and Solutions Associated with Prony’s Method for Processing Data with Pulse Noise
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Parametric spectral analysis methods such as the Prony’s method can provide precision far greater than Fourier transform-based methods for estimation of signals which conform to their model. One of the the main downsides of such methods can be their robustness when presented with noisy inputs. While classic white noise usually does not pose a problem for the calculations, more exotic types such as impulse noise can lead to a complete breakdown of the model. The paper explores the possibility of using additional algorithms to improve the Prony’s method’s ability to recover the signal parameters in the presence of a mix of white and impulse noise. These methods include the already known signal segmentation approach and the point skipping approach which can be considered the extreme form of the former. Basic auxiliary algorithm for impulse noise identification which relies on matched filtering-like approach and the use of the minimum duration principle is shown and applied during the testing. The methods are tested on digital models of signals and the best is then applied to real-world data obtained during radar scanning procedure.

articleTitle: Research of a Microstrip Antenna Array Excited by a Planar Waveguide with a quasi-TEM Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An antenna array based on patch radiators powered by quasi-TEM wave propagating in a planar waveguide (asymmetric microstrip line) is proposed. A comparative analysis of simulation and experiment results for a 7-element antenna array made of rectangular patch emitters is presented. The experimental sample of the antenna array is designed for the 5.8 GHz frequency range. The results of calculations of the amplification factor and the width of the main beam of the directional pattern of the antenna array in the E- and H-plane for 9, 11 and 21 elements are presented. A linear dependence of the width of the directional pattern in the E-plane and the gain coefficient on the number of elements of the antenna array is observed. Thus, a simple design of the antenna array with the possibility of adjusting the main radiation characteristics by selecting the required number of elements is proposed. It is shown that the gain factor of the 7-element array is 14.7 dBi, and the 21-element array has the gain of 20.5 dBi.

articleTitle: Development of Micro Brushless DC Motor Model Based on Project Design Calculation using Ansys Maxwell RMxprt
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The theoretical basis of Ansys Maxwell RMxprt software and modeling methods are considered. A method of project design calculation of a micro brushless direct current (BLDC) motor using Ansys Maxwell RMxprt software was developed for a manufactured motor with known overall dimensions and some passport data (rated voltage, rated speed, rated current, rated torque, rated power) of arbitrary power for the purpose of further parameterization of the BLDC motor model from the MATLAB Simulink library. This will allow the development of new models of micro electric drives and the synthesis of efficient micro BLDC control systems, which can improve their performance, accuracy and speed of operation. The calculation was carried out on the example of a specific Sinotech model BY35BL30 BLDC micromotor using Ansys Maxwell RMxprt software in accordance with the developed micro BLDC project design calculation methodology. The results obtained by the project design calculation using Ansys Maxwell RMxprt software coincide with the known original passport data of the manufactured BLDC micromotor with a small error of up to 5%. A comparative analysis of the results allows us to conclude about their high degree of coincidence. The use of this approach provides all the necessary parameters for the parameterization of the BLDC motor model from the MATLAB Simulink library. The research of the micro BLDC model in the Ansys Maxwell RMxprt software were carried out based on the data obtained during the project design calculation. Thus, the proposed approach has confirmed its workability and the assumption that it can be used for further research on electric drives based on BLDC.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Construction and Control System of the Robotic Mobile Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper considers the tasks of improving the construction and control system of a robotic mobile platform. A study of the features of reflective optical sensors operation in the control system of the mobile platform was carried out. The construction of the encoder and the control scheme of the servo drive for turning the wheels have been developed. The method of tracking the trajectory of the platform, given by the marking, is proposed.

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Navigation System Based on Ultrasonic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper authors propose the mobile robot and its navigation system development. This navigation system is based on two ultrasonic sensors HC-SR04. The device driver is developed. And the experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Computer analysis of the thermoelastic behavior of a steel rod with a thin copper coating during pulse electromagnetic action
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A physical-mathematical model for determination of the thermostressed state of a steel rod with a thin copper coating is proposed. The criteria for evaluating its performance based on the parameters of an external, non-stationary electromagnetic influence are established. Initial-boundary value problems for the considered rod are formulated to obtain the determining functions, including the axial component of the magnetic field intensity vector, temperature, and radial displacement vector. A technique for constructing solutions of these initial-boundary value problems is proposed, utilizing approximation of the distributions of the determining functions within the rod and coating by quadratic polynomials in the radial variable. Consequently, the original problems related to determining functions are transformed into corresponding time-dependent Cauchy problems involving integral characteristics of these functions with respect to the radial variable. The general solutions of the Cauchy problems under the consistent influence of a non-stationary electromagnetic field are determined. Based on the performed computer analysis, the regularities of changes in ponderomotive force, temperature, radial and circular stresses in the considered rod were analyzed under the impact of an electromagnetic pulse.

articleTitle: Acoustic Emission in a Bimaterial with an Internal Crack
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The dynamic problem of the displacement field in an elastic bimaterial, generated by time-stable displacements of the surfaces of a disk-shaped crack in one of its components, has been solved. The bimaterial is modeled as two ideally contacted layers with a mode III crack in one of them. The boundary integral equations method was used to solve the problem. The dependencies of displacements on the bimaterial surface on the wave number, on the distance between the observation point and the defect epicenter for different stiffness ratios of the bimaterial components, were established.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic Characteristics of Combined Slot Radiators as Elements of Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A problem of connecting three electrodynamic volumes with ideally conducting surfaces through narrow connecting slots and a radiating slot is solved in a rigorous electrodynamic formulation by the generalized method of induced magnetomotive forces (MMF). The solution is presented in an analytical form, taking into account the finite thickness of the walls of the connected volumes, in which slots are cut. The volumes are an infinite rectangular waveguide excited by the main wave, a rectangular resonator and a half-space above an infinite plane. The energy characteristics of this system have been comprehensively studied depending on the geometric dimensions and the relative positions of the constituent elements of the structure under consideration.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electromagnetic Pulse Scattering for Shape Reconstruction of Elliptical Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This study investigates the effectiveness of the use of electromagnetic (EM) pulses for object characterization and shape reconstruction by measurement of pulse echoes from the object in specific points. The near-field distribution of the total electric field is examined in order to optimize the incident pulse parameters. Additionally, an approach is introduced to estimate object shape. The results demonstrate the ability to accurately reconstruct shapes for elliptical cylinders.

articleTitle: Computer Analysis of Nonstationary Thermoelastic Processes in an Electrically Conductive Plate during Pulse Electromagnetic Treatment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A well-known physicomathematical model is used to determine temperature fields and stresses in a conductive plate under the action of pulsed electromagnetic fields (EMF). This model is based on the use of known experimental facts about the adiabatic processes of heating and deformation of a conductive body subjected to the action of pulsed EMF. On its basis, a non-stationary thermomechanics problem for a conductive non-ferromagnetic plate is formulated. General solutions to this problem for pulsed electromagnetic action have been obtained. A computer analysis of the obtained solutions was carried out, as a result of which the regularities of non-stationary thermomechanical processes in a conductive plate subjected to the action of electromagnetic pulses of microsecond duration have been investigated.

articleTitle: Approximate Solution of the Field Equations for Magnetodielectric Layer with Inhomogeneous Permeability on Perfectly Conducting Plane
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Based on the impedance concept, approximate solution of the equations for the field in magnetodielectric layer with inhomogeneous permeability on perfectly conducting plane is obtained. Graphs of the real and imaginary parts of the distributed surface impedance depending on layer thickness for linear law for the permeability change of the magnetodielectric are presented. The problem exact solution for the field in the layer is also presented for linear law of the permeability change.

articleTitle: Magnetic video-pulse impact on NMR spin echo signals of nuclei located in domain walls of magnets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The dependence of pinning force along the NMR spectrum of nuclei located in the domain walls of the face-centered-cubic (FCC) cobalt is studied in the cases of symmetrical and asymmetrical magnetic video-pulse (MVP) exposures. The pinning force does not depend on the character of the exposure in FCC cobalt and lithium-zinc ferrite. It is maximal in the center of the FCC cobalt NMR line, where the impact of MVP is minimal. The pinning force of these magnets along the NMR spectra is inversely proportional to the MVP amplitude at the fixed MVP duration. Besides it, the NMR line width in FCC cobalt is due to the anisotropic component of the hyperfine field on nuclei from the domain walls of FCC.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Multi-Element Line Array by the Amplitude of Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The 3D multielement system forming the electromagnetic field in far zone is build as a linear array of the semitransparent inclined mirrors. The systems geometry meets a quasi-optical condition. The separate mirrors of system are placed in a Fresnel zone, and the radiation pattern (RP) of the whole system is considered in its far zone. In order to simplify the solution of the direct electrodynamical problem, the separation of variables is supposed in the apertures of arrays. The above allows to derive the close formulas for the fields in the arrays of system and the total RP. The optimization problem consists of maximization of functional presenting weighted cross product of the given and created amplitude RPs. The opposite direction method is basic of the functional’s optimization. The computations demonstrate the ability to achieve the high-quality approximation to the desired RP.

articleTitle: Scattering of Elastic P/SV-Waves by an Elastic Fiber with Thin Interphase Layer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The scattering of elastic waves by the fiber contained in the matrix with the presence of an interfacial layer of variable thickness has been investigated. The elastic system is in dynamic plane deformation conditions. The thickness of the interlayer is small compared to the characteristic fiber size and the wavelengths propagating in the composite. The research algorithm is based on asymptotic modelling of the interaction of thin heterogeneity with surrounding bodies and the null-field method for solving the scattering problem. The influence of the mechanical and geometric parameters of the composite on the amplitude characteristics of P/SV-waves in the far wave zone, scattered by the fibrous non-canonical forms, was analyzed.

articleTitle: Modification of Characteristics of Bragg Structure Based on Chebyshev Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Bragg-type layered dielectric structure, which provides the Chebyshev character of the behavior of the reflection frequency response, was considered. To obtain a fractional-rational representation of the structure frequency response, method of synthesis of the type I Chebyshev filter was used. An approach for mapping the entire equiripple domain of Chebyshev polynomial onto the specified reflectionless band and determining scale parameter are proposed. A modification of the periodic Bragg-type layered structure is demonstrated, which provides a reflection frequency response with minimum ripple level in the passband while preserving the location of the zeros that delimit the reflection band of the structure.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of Solutions of the Hammerstein Equation in the Class of Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The numerical results of the polynomial solution of the optimization problem with a free phase are presented. The case of a complex polynomial of the first degree is considered. This polynomial shows good approximation characteristics of the optimization nonlinear functional.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model for Plate Elastic Properties Studying Based on Its Amplitude-Frequency Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: the article describes a mathematical model for studying the elastic properties of a plate on its amplitude-frequency characteristics under the influence of an external disturbance. The methods of nonlinear mechanics were used to build the mathematical model. Based on the obtained equations, graphical dependences of amplitude-frequency characteristics for soft, linear, and rigid systems are constructed. The obtained results can be used in future studies of oscillatory processes in resonators.

articleTitle: Development of a Control System for a Vibratory Lapping-Polishing Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Vibratory equipment is widely used in various fields of mechanical, industrial, and manufacturing engineering. Particularly, such machines can be effectively implemented while carrying out finishing technological operations, e.g., glazing, polishing, and lapping of different machine parts. The present paper is focused on developing the control system for the novel design of a vibratory lapping-polishing machine driven by six solenoids. The main purpose consists in providing the circular trajectory of the working member and ensuring the machining uniformity at each point of the surface being treated. In such a case, it is proposed to actuate the solenoids with the specified time shift depending on the forced frequency needed to be provided. The duration of the signal actuating the solenoid is equal to one-sixth of the total duration of a cycle (period) of the working body oscillation. The corresponding control approach is developed and simulated in the Tinkercad application, while the control system is designed based on the Arduino hardware and software. In addition, the laboratory prototype of the vibratory lapping-polishing machine and the corresponding control system are implemented in practice. The performed laboratory studies and experimental tests substantiate the possibilities of generating the circular oscillations of the working member of the vibration-driven lapping-polishing machine. The obtained results may be useful for engineers and technologists dealing with control systems of various vibratory technological equipment based on electromagnetic and solenoid-type drives.

articleTitle: Forming a Sector Radiation Pattern of a Dipole Antenna Placed Parallel to Metal Square Screen
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In telecommunication systems, it is required to take into account the specifics of a working area of particular system and to exclude the areas in which the transmission of information is disturbed. To meet such requirements, it is usually needed to provide the amplitude of the useful signal is not lower than –3 dB of the main lobe maximum, within the entire operating frequency band. This paper considers the asymptotic solution of the diffraction 3D vector problem of a half–wave dipole field placed parallel to a square screen. It is investigated a forming of the Radiation Pattern (RP) of a sector shape by choosing corresponding distance between the screen and the dipole h. It is shown that these optimal distances depend on the screen sizes. Using the developed software, the optimal dipole–screen spacing h, which provide a sector shape RPs, has been determined with a dependence on the screen sizes. Corresponding RPs have been calculated as well.

articleTitle: The Method of Auxiliary Sources in Applied Electrodynamics Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This article presents an overview of our works in applied electrodynamics using the Method of Auxiliary Sources (MAS). The details of the correct selection of auxiliary parameters for efficient use of the MAS are presented. The importance to consider Scattered Field Singularities (SFS) is discussed. Considering SFS and some recommendations based on many years of experience, the MAS is expanded for large body and large scenarios scattering, eigenfields, and eigenvalues problems as well as inverse problems solution, sharply minimizing at the same time the required computational resources.

articleTitle: Cloaking Study of Metal Surface by Liquid Foam Structures in the Millimeter Range
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This work is devoted to the study of the characteristics of cloaking by halp of reflection of electromagnetic waves of the millimeter range from dynamic foam structures. This topic has been studied very little because of its complexity, because dynamic foam structures are not stable, they are formed on the basis of foam-forming liquids, which means that they constantly disintegrate within a short time. This requires a very short time of measurements and processing of experimental data. The multi-frequency method of measurement and fast Fourier transformation is used for the research. The method was implemented on an experimental measuring and computing complex in the frequency range from 38 to 52 GHz. Which allows to separately study the reflection from the front and back faces of foam structure samples. Foam samples were produced on a foam generator, which made it possible to obtain structures with quasi-one-dimensional inhomogeneities in the form of bubbles. The obtained research results showed that in the range of millimeter waves, the reflection value is very small, from 0,00001 to 0,056. It is the smaller value of reflection not from the beginning of foam formation, and not at the end of its existence, but in the middle of the time existence of the foam structure. The results of the research can be useful for the development of low-reflective and cloaking coatings.

articleTitle: Multipole Representation of Tesseral and Sectoral Spherical Wave Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This work deals with study of multipole structures describing the tesseral and sectoral spherical wave functions. Such functions are known to occur in three-dimensional boundary value problems of electrodynamics and can be identified by field potentials. They also have a multipole character and can be represented as a set of monopole fields. The paper poses the problem of determining the structure of such multipoles.

articleTitle: Estimation of Eigenfrequencies of Ultrasonic Transducers in Pulse-echo Method
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Resonance properties of the transducers of ultrasound non-destructive testing system are investigated. The system for non-contact reflective ultrasonic testing is described. The model of the ratio of polynomials is used in the frequency domain. Some improvement to combination of Levy and Gauss-Newton methods for finding natural frequency of the transducers are proposed. Several versions of rational approximation of frequency characteristics are compared.

articleTitle: Energy Transformation of Transient Radiation of Plane Source with Step-Like Excitation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The energy conversion near an aperture radiator is investigated for the case of the transient excitation. The case of uniform distribution of current with step-like time dependence is presented for analysis. The analytical solution of the problem in time domain based on the evolutionary approach is used for analysis of wave energy transformation. The change of energy flux for different distances from source is calculated numerically. The expressions for total energy of the wave is obtained analytically. It is illustrated the transforming of the total energy into static part and wave.

articleTitle: On the Spectral Properties of Uryson Integral Equation Depended on Two Numerical Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The generalization of the nonlinear integral equation of the Uryson type is considered, which consists in introducing two real numerical parameters into the integrant. This makes it possible to find in the given area multiple points of possible branching (bifurcation) of solutions in the form of spectral lines by solving a nonlinear two-parameter spectral problem.

articleTitle: Measurement and Evaluation of the EM Field Impact in the Range of 4G/5G Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The aim of paper is to extract the spectral frequency radiation in the range of 4G operations. The experimental setup, supplemented by spectrum analyzer USB-SA44B supplemented by the respective software, notebook for analysis of signals, transmitting-receiving antenna array consisting of four microstrip antennas, the transmitting antenna operating in the frequencies 0.9 GHz, 1.8 GHz and 2.45 GHz, and signal generator SA6 is used for the measurements. The designed setup demonstrates the possibility to extract the spectral characteristics of radiation in the range of 4G operations. It is observed that the fixed strength of radiation depends on the sources of radiation. The perspective of design is evaluation of the SAR at the laboratory environment.

articleTitle: Dynamic Interaction Effects for One-Periodic Array of Rigid Disc-Shaped Inclusions in 3D Elastic Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An explanation is provided for the boundary integral formulation of 3D problems involving the incidence of normal time-harmonic longitudinal waves on a single-periodic array of coplanar rigid disc-shaped inclusions. The translation of the inclusions as rigid units and the dynamic stress intensity factor in the inclusion vicinities, specifically in mode-II, are computed and analyzed based on variations in the wave number, periodic distance, and mass of the constituent inclusions.

articleTitle: Effects of Seawater Pollution on Wireless Signals: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Seawater pollution is a significant hazard to marine ecosystems and humans, requiring immediate attention and effective mitigation techniques. The present review paper investigates the complex link between seawater pollution and wireless signal transmission, examining the possible interplay, difficulties, and possibilities resulting from this interaction. The research investigated the numerous contaminants that affect maritime ecosystems, such as chemical compounds, microplastics, and oil spills, and analyzed their effects on wireless signal propagation. The impacts of signal interference produced by pollution exponentially grow and decrease wireless communication in terms of network performance in coastal locations, would be paramount to achieving accurate marine life. However, prospects for research and development in this field have been explored to underline the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration to overcome complex issues. The review study's goal is to foster a deeper understanding of the relationship between seawater pollution and wireless signal propagation domains and provide valuable insights to researchers, policymakers, and stakeholders working to preserve and manage our marine ecosystems.

articleTitle: Total Input Current of the Cylindrical Radiator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: It was proposed the method for calculating the total input current of a cylindrical linear radiator. The input current is equal to the sum of the terms of the series obtained as result of solving the Leontovich’s integral equation by expanding in powers of a small parameter. The total current is determined as the result of adding the first term of the series and the sum of an infinite geometric progression. Recommendations are given on the application of the proposed method to other integral equations for the current in antennas.

articleTitle: Reception of UWB Pulsed Electromagnetic Fields : Ferrite antenna with a two-turns coil
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper introduces the utilization of spiral windings for converting the electromagnetic field of an incident on an antenna pulse electromagnetic waves into electrical signals at the output of the UWB impulse antenna. Employing mathematical modeling via the Finite-Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method, we investigated the transient response of the receiving antenna when an incident pulsed signal has a step-like amplitude-time dependence. We studied the impact of geometric parameters of the windings and load resistance on the amplitude-time and energy characteristics of a wideband pulsed-receiving ferrite antenna.

articleTitle: Loop and Folded Antenna with Large Dimensions and Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: It is considered the method of calculating a metal loop antenna with large dimensions. It is proposed the antenna with in-phase current distribution and with properties like the properties of a loop antenna. This antenna allows to obtain higher electrical characteristics. The described method is applied to the proposed antenna and to folded radiator with capacitors.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Scattering by Half-plane with Fractional Boundary Conditions Using Legendre Polynomials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The present study investigates a classical problem with different solution approaches. The E-polarized electromagnetic scattering by half-plane with fractional boundary conditions via two different methods is studied and the results are compared. The outcomes reveal that Legendre exponential functions are suitable as a complete set to express the induced current densities on the scatterer after several mathematical manipulations. The current and field distributions for different parameters are provided when the fractional order becomes 0.5 an 1.

articleTitle: Multipole Representation of Zonal Spherical Wave Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The work is devoted to the study of multipole structures that describe the zonal spherical wave functions. Such functions are encountered in some three-dimensional boundary problems of electrodynamics, and they have the meaning of field potentials. These functions have a multipole character and can be represented as a set of monopole fields. The goal is to determine the structures of such multipoles.

articleTitle: Multipole Representation of Certain Cylindrical Wave Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This work deals with study of multipole structures, that describe the high order circular cylinder wave functions, which are encountered in number of two-dimensional boundary problems of electrodynamics. As is known, these functions have a multipole character and can be represented as a set of monopole fields. Several possible multipole structures for the considered functions are found in this work.

articleTitle: Managing Electromagnetic Interference in Access Control Card Readers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Access control systems are an essential component of modern security infrastructure, providing a secure means of restricting access to sensitive areas. Access control card readers are vulnerable to electromagnetic interference (EMI), which can cause system malfunction, downtime, and even system failure. This paper discusses guidelines provided by IEEE for managing EMI in electronic access control systems, including selecting and installing card readers that meet electromagnetic compatibility standards, installing card readers away from EMI sources, using proper cabling, ensuring proper grounding, regularly inspecting and maintaining the system, and implementing shielding techniques. The paper also covers different types of card readers, cabling, and shielding, along with their benefits and limitations [1].

articleTitle: The Band Properties of Resonant Dipole Antennas Placed Parallel to Finite Size Flat Screen
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In the paper it is considered the resonant dipole of length 2l located parallel to a perfectly conducting square screen. By the uniform geometrical theory of diffraction is investigated the impact of the screen dimensions to the antennas band properties. Using the developed software, it has been calculated: the radiation patterns (RPs), the directivity in the direction of normal to the screen, the radiation resistance and the Back to Front Ratio depending on the wavelength and the screen size, varied in a wide bounds. It is shown that the half–power beam width of the RP's main lobe slightly depends on the screen sizes. The Back to Front Ratio and the level of side lobes are the lower, the larger the screen size is. Also the resonant nature of the directivity and the radiation resistance relations has been found. The maximum directivity values in the entire wave band are achievable at the electrical screen sizes of 0.7 ÷ 1.3. With increasing operating wavelength from half to one and half of central one, the maximum values of directivity are changed from 2.5 to 8.9 relative units and corresponding screen size is increased too. The values of radiation resistance have the resonance in a narrow range of the electrical screen sizes of 0.7 ÷ 0.9. Meanwhile it is decreased by an order of magnitude for wavelengths greater than one and half of the central one, regardless of the screen size. In terms of the band properties, a dipole antenna with an ideally conducting screen can be classified as ultra–wideband.

articleTitle: Dielectric Cylinder Discrimination with ANN Using Wideband Electromagnetic Response
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The application of three-component stacked artificial neural networks (ANN) for discrimination of dielectric cylinders of different diameters by their radio images is considered. Neural networks include two sparse autoencoders and the softmax unit. Neural networks are not tied to the frequency range, unlike many well-known methods based on the resonant properties of objects, and they are a powerful tool for object recognition. Radio images were obtained using the method of auxiliary sources (MAS) for cylinders with the radius of 15 to 35 mm. The possibility of successful recognition was confirmed for the case of the diameter deviation of 1 mm and the presence of additive Gaussian noise with SNR of up to 5 dB.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Heating Regimes of a Steel Strip by a Quasi-Steady Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A two-dimensional physical and mathematical model is proposed for studying the laws of induction heating of a steel strip by a quasi-steady electromagnetic field. A two-dimensional non-stationary problem of electrodynamics is formulated for an electrically conductive strip of rectangular section under the action of a homoheneous non-stationary electromagnetic field. The component of the magnetic field strength vector tangential to the front surfaces of the strip was chosen as the determining function. The boundary conditions for matching the values of the determining function at the corner points of the rectangle of the cross-section of the strip, that is, the boundary conditions on its edges, are recorded. To construct the solution of the formulated problem, double finite integral transformations over the thickness and transverse coordinates of the strip and the Laplace integral transformation over time were used. As a result, the expression of the determining function in the form of a double functional series is obtained. The change in Joule heat at the characteristic points of the cross-section of the steel strip was numerically analyzed depending on the characteristic dimensionless time and the parameter characterizing the penetration depth of induction heating currents relative to the half-thickness of the strip. Two limiting cases of near-surface and continuous heating of the strip by an external quasi-steady electromagnetic field are considered.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic nonreciprocity in a reflectarray composed of nonlinear resonant elements
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Resonant nonspecular reflection by a planar periodic structure constructed of short circular cylinders placed on a silver substrate has been simulated. Our research is focused on electromagnetic nonreciprocity that manifests itself for direct and reversed scenarios of reflection in the first diffraction order of the nonlinear cylinder array. Full-wave numerical simulation were performed and spectral reflection characteristics were obtained for different values of incident electromagnetic wave intensity. We have also studied the distribution of fields in the cylinders at reflection resonances and its effect on the degree of nonreciprocity in the direct and reversed scenarios. At frequencies where magnetic dipole moments arise from the circular displacement currents in the cylinders, nonreciprocity is more pronounced than in other types of resonant field distribution in discs.

articleTitle: GUI-Based Dielectric Elliptical Cylinder Parameters Optimization for Front Echo Reduction in Pulse Scattering Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This article proposes a novel numerical approach to reduce scattering echoes in the front area of dielectric objects using a Gaussian radio pulse covering a frequency range of 6-12 GHz. The approach optimizes the dimensions and dielectric permittivity of an elliptical cylinder to ensure the incident pulse create practically no echoes in the front region. A newly developed user-friendly graphical user interface program package facilitates the optimization process, allowing to explore different geometries and permittivity configurations with the slider in its interface and achieve minimal echo in the front region, thus enhancing the invisibility or reduced detectability of dielectric objects in various scenarios.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Specific Absorption Rate for a Honey bee Exposed to Radiofrequency Electromagnetic Fields from 2.5 to 100 GHz
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents a study of electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure of a honey bee at radio frequencies from 2.5 GHz to 100 GHz using numerical simulations based on the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique. The main goal of our study was to estimate the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) in honey bee tissues as a dosimetric aid to predict the possible adverse effects caused by EMF energy absorption. In this study, the insect is modeled as a 3-tissue heterogeneous dielectric object, and the Sim4Life EM-FDTD solver was used for EM simulations. The whole-body and brain tissue-averaged SAR values of a honeybee were determined for all considered frequencies and normalized on 1 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> incident plane-wave power density. The obtained SAR values were also averaged over a volume of 1 milligram of tissue. The results showed that EMF energy absorption in insects depends on E-field polarization, frequency, and the insect’s body peculiarities.

articleTitle: Coupling Induced Resonantly Enhanced Scattering Properties of Wedge-Channel Nanoparticle Dimers and Trimers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXVIII International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This work is devoted to investigation of the plasmon resonance coupling effects in dimer and trimer of such nanoparticles (NPs), one of those may have Wedge Plasmon Polariton, while another may have Channel Plasmon Polariton, when Gap Plasmon Polariton also appears due to the NP coupling. The main interest is to investigate the dependence of such effects on distance between NPs in dimer and trimer, as well as to find optimal distance to obtain the best possible resonantly enhanced scattering properties. For this purpose, in this work numerical simulation scheme is proposed, which is based on Spectral Fourier-Galerkin Boundary Integral Equation method with Analytical Regularization involving Singularity Subtraction, enhanced by Fast Fourier Transform (FFT).
